checks.expected_narration: Check the energy values first. The clean table gives zero point three one five, zero point three six zero, and zero point three seven five. The centered slope is the right energy minus the left energy, divided by zero point two. That gives zero point three. The center log ratio is zero point five four minus zero point two four, also zero point three. The clean residual is zero. After changing the last log gamma two, the right-hand energy becomes zero point four. The centered slope is then zero point four two five. Subtract the unchanged center log ratio of zero point three, leaving a residual of positive zero point one two five. Finite differences depend on spacing, rounding, and noise. Our hand calculation assumes equal spacing; the lab's three-point formula also handles unequal spacing. Neither a single residual nor a small averaged score establishes a universal certificate. Keep your corrections, then open Lab guide pages two and three for the demonstration.
